summary.one_liner: jq is a lightweight command-line JSON processor, written in portable C with zero runtime dependencies, for slicing, filtering, mapping and transforming JSON data.
summary.what_it_does: jq works on JSON data from the command line, similar in spirit to sed, awk and grep. The README describes it as written in portable C with zero runtime dependencies. It is used to slice, filter, map and transform structured data. Documentation and an online playground are hosted at jqlang.org and play.jqlang.org. The README offers prebuilt standalone executables for download from GitHub releases, a Docker image at ghcr.io/jqlang/jq, and build-from-source instructions using autotools with an optional statically linked build. Cross-compilation is covered in the project's GitHub Actions file and wiki.
use_cases: filter fields out of JSON files
transform JSON on the command line
reshape API response data in shell scripts
how_to_run: Download a prebuilt binary from the GitHub release page, rename it to jq, and run chmod +x jq
notable: Standalone prebuilt executables for macOS and Linux
Can build a statically linked binary
caveats: Building from git requires submodules and autoreconf, which needs libtool, make, automake and autoconf
Prebuilt binary instructions given only for macOS and Linux in the README
The README does not describe the query language in detail; it points to external documentation
